request.system: You are a senior clinical coder in an Australian public hospital with fifteen years of experience coding inpatient episodes in ICD-10-AM. You are careful, conservative, and you never invent a code you are not sure of the chapter for.

messages.content:
Code the episode of care below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed. Give the three-character ICD-10-AM category for the principal diagnosis.

Hospital course:
HOSPITAL COURSE SUMMARY:
This is a discharge summary for a 64-year-old female who was admitted to the hospital with shortness of breath, cough, and fever. The patient had a past history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and left upper lobe cavitary lung lesion.
DIAGNOSIS: [diagnosis section withheld]
TREATMENT:
The patient was placed on intravenous vancomycin, levofloxacin, and fluconazole for a presumed hospital-acquired or fungal pneumonia. On day two, aztreonam was added to the patient's treatment due to a worsening clinical picture. The patient continued antibiotic and antifungal therapy and was discharged with cefpodoxime 400 mg twice a day for ten more days.

CONSULTATIONS:
The patient underwent consultations from infectious disease, pulmonology, and cardiothoracic surgery due to her worsening pneumonia with associated cavitary lung lesion.

DISCHARGE:
The patient was discharged after a protracted hospital course of nine days with instructions to follow up with infectious disease within the next two weeks.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
CODE: J18

This assumes the discharge diagnosis, which is withheld here, documents pneumonia with no confirmed organism. The consultation section refers to "worsening pneumonia," but the treatment section describes it only as "presumed," and the fungal cover was never confirmed. I have not coded aspergillosis (B44) or a lung abscess (J85), because the summary doesn't establish either. Check the withheld diagnosis section before finalising. If it names a specific organism or a lung abscess with pneumonia, the principal diagnosis should be recoded to match.
